concerns.text: The plan treats the computed Minimum Detectable Effect Size (MDES) as a proxy for ‘adequate power’ by counting studies with MDES ≤ 0.5 (see step 5 and SC‑002). MDES is a deterministic function of sample size, α and target power; it is not a measure of the study’s actual power nor of whether the study was sufficiently powered for its observed effect. Using an arbitrary MDES threshold (0.5) to declare a study ‘adequately powered’ is not justified in the statistical literature and conflates two distinct concepts (design‑level detectability vs. achieved power). This constitutes a scientifically unsound claim and makes the primary evaluation circular: the outcome (MDES ≤ 0.5) is directly derived from the predictor (sample size) without independent validation.
